clue.text: European partner, so-called

definitions.meaning: a native of the Netherlands, a Hollander
in Cockney usage 'my old ...' is a man's wife, so a partner as she is called in slang

explanation.surface: Someone introduces their so-called partner from elsewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' as Cockney slang for a wife comes from 'duchess'; 'so-called' flags that it is a nickname rather than a dictionary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a nationality adjective for Holland, and London slang for a spouse.

clue.text: Intended, say, to leave husband outside the emporium

indicators.note: the leave and husband words wrap round the sound of intended

parts.note: to depart is to leave
to husband resources is to store them up

indicators.note: say tells us the word for intended is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: A fiancee plans to walk out on her husband in front of a big shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intended' suggests a fiancee, but it is MEANT, which said aloud gives MENT; 'husband' is a verb meaning to save, STORE.
explanation.definitionFit: An emporium is a large shop selling many kinds of goods.

clue.text: Drawn out of line, like the walls in Mah-jong?

indicators.note: the tied word is stretched out around the line letter

parts.note: a drawn match is tied

explanation.surface: Mah-jong pieces are pulled out of their row in the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: In Mah-jong players build a 'wall' of tiles before play; the question mark marks the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall covered in square ceramic pieces is described as tiled, and the Mah-jong wall is built of such pieces.

clue.text: Shock treatment for a page-boy, perhaps

definitions.text: Shock treatment for a page-boy, perhaps

parts.words: Shock treatment for a page-boy, perhaps
parts.note: a shock is a mass of hair and a page-boy is a bob hairstyle, so the treatment is a visit to the barber

explanation.surface: A young servant in a hotel receives electric shock therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock treatment' suggests medicine; a shock is a thick head of hair, and a page-boy is a style of cut.
explanation.definitionFit: The barber's trim, which might produce a page-boy style.

clue.text: Reviewing amount of money the china raised

parts.note: a sum is an amount of money
Ming is a famous dynasty of Chinese porcelain
up means raised or lifted

explanation.surface: Someone tallies what a piece of porcelain fetched when it was put up for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: MING is porcelain from China's Ming dynasty, so 'the china' points to it; the capital-free 'china' hides that.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge's summary of the case at the end of a trial is a review of the evidence.

clue.text: Composer, not one to overindulge

indicators.note: not tells us the letter for one is missing from the composer

parts.note: Erik Satie was a French composer
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A composer is described as someone who never overindulges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not one to overindulge' reads as a temperate person, but 'not one' removes I from SATIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To glut or surfeit is to fill to excess.

clue.text: Flower, maybe, lost some pieces finally falling off

indicators.note: the final letter of each of the three pieces drops away

explanation.surface: A flower, perhaps, has shed some petals at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces finally falling off' removes the last letters E, T and E from MAYBE, LOST and SOME, leaving MAYB, LOS and SOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawthorn blossom, which flowers in late spring, is a flower.

clue.text: One privy to secrets imprisoned by king

parts.note: inside is slang for in prison
R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king locks up someone who knows too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imprisoned by' looks like a container, but the pieces sit side by side: INSIDE then R.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone within an organisation who has access to confidential knowledge.

clue.text: Church high-ups spouting from the gutter!

definitions.text: Church high-ups spouting from the gutter!

parts.words: Church high-ups spouting from the gutter!
parts.note: church high-ups sounds like senior clergy talking foully, but these are carved creatures high on a church that spout rainwater from the guttering

explanation.surface: Senior clergy use vulgar language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-ups' are things placed high on the building, and 'spouting from the gutter' is literal water, not coarse talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Grotesque carved stone waterspouts on churches carry rain from the roof gutters.

clue.text: Books about religious education heartily deplore the making of images

indicators.note: the books word wraps round the education letters and the heart of deplore

parts.note: publications are books
RE is religious education, a school subject

indicators.note: heartily means take the heart, the middle letter, of deplore

explanation.surface: Books about religious education strongly lament the creation of idols.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartily' reads as 'strongly' but picks L, the middle letter of DEPLORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Publicity work consists of creating and managing a favourable image for a client.

clue.text: For which a lifeline is essential at the seaside

definitions.text: For which a lifeline is essential at the seaside

parts.words: For which a lifeline is essential at the seaside
parts.note: a lifeline sounds like a rescue rope by the sea, but here it is the crease on a hand read by fortune-tellers on seaside piers

explanation.surface: A lifeline seems vital for safety on a beach.
explanation.walkthrough: The life line is one of the creases read in a hand; seaside piers and promenades traditionally have fortune-tellers' booths.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading the lines of the hand, including the life line, is the fortune-teller's art.

clue.text: Cancel membership fees, being out of credit

indicators.note: the fee word sits outside, so the credit letters are found inside it

parts.note: a sub, short for subscription, is a membership fee

explanation.surface: A member cancels their subscription after running short of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being out of' reads as lacking credit, but it says the fee word lies outside CR.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub a plan is informal for calling it off.

clue.text: Doctor cured sweetheart needed to lose weight

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the heart, or middle letter, of the word sweet is E

explanation.surface: A physician tells a patient whose sweetheart wants them slimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun but is a verb signalling the rearrangement of CURED.
explanation.definitionFit: To slim is to cut down one's weight, the dieting sense.

clue.text: Very willing to shorten one of these flowers?

definitions.text: Very willing to shorten one of these flowers?

parts.words: Very willing to shorten one of these flowers?
parts.note: glad means very willing, and glad is also the short name gardeners give these blooms, so being happy to shorten them is apt

explanation.surface: A gardener happily trims a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: Gardeners call these tall blooms 'glads' for short, and glad also means willing.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of the sword-lily, tall flowering plants of the iris family.

clue.text: Language bound to make one too embarrassed to speak

parts.note: a tongue is a language
tied means bound

explanation.surface: A language seems certain to leave a learner speechless with shyness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to' looks like 'certain to', but 'bound' is TIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unable to talk from shyness, as if the speaking organ were fastened down.

clue.text: Grotesque giant

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both the hideous and the colossal.

clue.text: Self regarding youth Russians caught misbehaving

indicators.note: misbehaving means acting wrongly, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A vain young man is caught by some Russians while behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the youth of Greek myth who fell in love with his own reflection.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the youth fell for his own reflection in a pool, the type of vanity.

clue.text: Left with king at end of game, it can help one draw

indicators.note: the left and king letters are placed after the game letters

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game
ER, Edward Rex, stands for a king

explanation.surface: A chess player is left with only the king when the game ends.
explanation.walkthrough: ER usually means the Queen (Elizabeth Regina) but can equally be Edward Rex, a king; 'draw' suggests a drawn chess game, not sketching.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight-edged strip guides the pencil in drawing lines.

clue.text: One acts on impulse, showing courage

definitions.meaning: a fibre in the body that carries electrical signals

explanation.surface: An impulsive person is praised for bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the body's signal-carrying fibre and boldness in the face of danger.

clue.text: Allow mistake to nettle one

indicators.note: a mistake is something done wrong, so these letters are put in the wrong order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone permits an error to annoy a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nettle' looks like a verb meaning annoy; it is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a right or permission to do something.

clue.text: Dregs the Spanish birds eat

parts.note: coffee grounds are dregs, the sediment left behind
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Birds peck at what is left in the bottom of a Spanish cup.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a verb phrase: the answer is a weed whose seeds are fed to cage birds.
explanation.definitionFit: This common weed is traditional food for canaries and other cage birds.

clue.text: In no state to accept, for example, a bunch of flowers

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the phrase meaning no say takes in the example letters

parts.note: to state is to say

explanation.surface: Someone is in no condition to receive, say, a bouquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' reads as a condition, but it is a verb, SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A small posy of sweet-smelling blooms.

clue.text: Use it to get capital, vital after move

indicators.note: the word for vital follows the word for move

parts.note: to shift is to move
key means vital or crucial

explanation.surface: Raising capital is vital after relocating a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money, but it is a capital letter on a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding down this keyboard button gives upper-case letters.

clue.text: Fairy's bound to come first for liveliness

indicators.note: the bound, or boundary, of the fairy word is its last letter, which now moves to the front

parts.note: a sprite is a fairy or elf

explanation.surface: A fairy is sure to arrive first, full of spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' reads as 'certain', but it is the boundary, the end letter E of SPRITE, which moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The French loan word means wit and spirited vivacity.

clue.text: Rule not all dare ignore

indicators.note: not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A regime that nobody dares to defy.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's period of sovereignty is their rule.

clue.text: Muffler endlessly wound

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the scarf word is cut off

parts.note: a muffler is a scarf

explanation.surface: A scarf is wrapped round and round without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' reads as the past of wind, matching a scarf wrapped round, but it is the noun: an injury mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark left on the skin by a healed injury.

clue.text: Attack from the kickoff

definitions.meaning: an assault, as in the ... of the enemy

explanation.surface: A team launches an assault straight from the start of the match.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an assault and the beginning of something.

clue.text: Unknown coin got in change

indicators.note: change suggests coins, but here it means alter the order of these letters

explanation.surface: An unidentified coin has turned up among some loose change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' seems to be small coins, matching 'coin'; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling under a false name means being unrecognised.

clue.text: Sweetheart as loving as a TV character

parts.note: the heart, or middle letter, of sweet is E
tender means loving and gentle

explanation.surface: A sweetheart is described as being as affectionate as a soap star.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a long-running BBC soap set in the East End of London; one of its characters is an East Ender.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident of London's East End, the setting of a BBC soap, so any figure in that soap.

clue.text: Chatters loudly about North Americans

indicators.note: the chatter word goes round the letter for north

parts.note: to yak is to chatter noisily

explanation.surface: Someone talks loudly about people from North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North' joins 'Americans' in the surface but is only the letter N.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal name for people from the United States.
